J. MacFlynn 'was unanimously re-elected chairman' and congratulated 'the five members of the old Council who successfully defended their seats' (Derry Journal, 9 June 1964, p. 5, image read)

note: Triennial election of Limavady Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. There were 29 nominations for the 23 seats (Londonderry Sentinel, 20 May 1964, p. 1); the five divisions polled were Ballyharrigan, Bellarena, Dungiven, Feeny and Owenreagh, where 'All the five outgoing members ... were returned ... in straight fights' (Londonderry Sentinel, 10 June 1964, p. 15). Scriggan was not polled: Mr. William McFarlane (Unionist) was nominated against the outgoing chairman, but the poll was held in only the five divisions above, and Dr. MacFlynn was re-elected chairman at the new council's meeting on 8 June 1964 (Derry Journal, 9 June 1964, p. 5). The withdrawal itself is not reported in the papers searched. Returned unopposed.
